### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

when I open the current file I'm in with mini files using

```lua
MiniFiles.open(bufname, false)
MiniFiles.reveal_cwd()
```

for example im in test.lua file, I open the current file in mini files, then I delete it, it moves it to the special trash directory, a new lua_ls server is started. I think this is happening because after the file is deleted and moved to the special trash directory, the file/buffer is still open but in the new trash directory, thus a new lsp starts in this new file that is in the trash directory even though I'm still in mini files. This happens with my other lsps as well. potential fix could maybe be deleting the buffer when the file is deleted?

these are my mini files options

```lua
options = {
    use_as_default_explorer = false,
    permanent_delete = false,
},
mappings = {
    go_in = "l",
    go_in_plus = "<CR>",
    go_out = "h",
    go_out_plus = "-",
},
content = {
    filter = function(entry)
        return entry.fs_type ~= "file" or entry.name ~= ".DS_Store"
    end,
},
windows = {
    width_focus = 20,
    width_nofocus = 20,
    width_preview = 20,
    preview = true,
},
```

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe.
   Feel free to include images/videos/etc, this helps a lot.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

Thanks for the issue!

I can't reproduce per se (with `lua_ls`), maybe some options on how the server acts are different. But I can see this happening. Just to be sure, could you please share how you have `lua_ls` set up?

At the moment, deleting a file that is associated with currently opened buffer does not lead to also do delete/wipeout the buffer. And I think it is a good thing, mostly as a safety measure while explicitly wiping out the buffer is not much trouble.

I'll think about the best approach to handle this.

> Also just one more thing, is it possible to have an option passed in for mini files that allows it to be not closed when another window is opened/focused, right now mini files closes when I open vim.ui.select or vim.ui.input and causes them to close as well, which I have some use cases for with lsp rename.

It is possible to implement, of course, but it is not there for a reason to not overcomplicate the logic. Right now it autocloses to handle the case of user accidentally using `:quit` or mouse clicking outside of the explorer. As described, for example, [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1292#issuecomment-2423837992).

Could you describe the use cases you have in mind?

As described, for example, [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1292#issuecomment-2423837992).
> 
> Could you describe the use cases you have in mind?

Thanks for the examples, I got it working for my use case so no need to implement the option to avoid closing! I had a use case where there would be vim.ui.select showing up to confirm whether or not to modify the import paths of the renamed file when renaming a file using mini files.

I did not manage to reproduce the LSP part specifically, but (hopefully) it should now be resolved on latest `main`.

The buffer for the file that has moved to trash is now not renamed. This makes it both more similar to permanent delete behavior and should not trigger any autocommands (which I think was a the culprit of attaching new LSP server).

Would you mind updating to latest `main` and check if it works for you now?
